# skill: simplify

Use to cut extras nobody needs yet. Not Claude Code simplify

# simplify — make it simple so a first-time reader can follow

> **One rule:** someone not on this work, opening it 6 months from now, must understand it and continue it without asking anyone.

## Use when
- Any work handed to people (code, documents, plans, designs, slides, tables, answers) may hold more than the task needs.
- Cutting a spec, plan or architecture to the fewest parts: also open [`references/architecture-and-anti-patterns.md`](references/architecture-and-anti-patterns.md).
- `human-writing` controls how it is written; this skill controls what the work contains.

Not for: Claude Code's own `/simplify` command · more detail on code (if installed) → `lazy-coding` · `readable-code` in plugin `software-development`.

## Steps
1. Climb the ladder and stop at the first step that works: (a) is this really needed? If not, do not do it and say in 1 line what you skipped; (b) is there an existing thing that works (file, template, function, tool, built-in feature)? Use it; (c) do the shortest version that is still complete and correct.
2. Do only what the task needs; cut before adding (if removing a part loses neither meaning nor function, cut it); plain things people know beat clever things that need decoding.
3. Apply by kind of work:
   - **Code:** names say what it is and carry units · 1 function does 1 thing · return early instead of nesting `if` · at most 3 levels of indentation · comments say why · follow the project's style. Avoid an abstraction with one user, clever hard-to-read shortcuts, one big file, a pile-up `utils/`, a new dependency for a few lines.
   - **Documents · reports:** conclusion first · 1 paragraph 1 topic · an example for abstract points · a table for compared data. Avoid repeats, empty headings, unknown terms.
   - **Plans · procedures:** 3–5 key items, each with an owner and a way to measure done · fewest steps that work. Avoid a 20-item list with no priority.
   - **Designs · slides · figures:** 1 page 1 point · shortest path to the user's goal · familiar patterns. Avoid cramming and decoration that does not help.
   - **Tables · data:** only columns used to decide · short formulas. Avoid columns that repeat a meaning and long nested formulas.
   - **Answers:** answer first, as long as the question needs.
4. **Simple is not sloppy:** never cut correctness, safety, validation of data from outside, error handling that prevents data loss, or what the user asked for explicitly. **Simple is not one big pile:** keep clear separation of duties, 1 part doing 1 thing.
5. When you take a deliberate shortcut, write how far it works and when it changes, for example `// simple: เก็บใน memory — ย้ายไป Redis เมื่อรันเกิน 1 process`, and put 1 line in the report: `ข้าม: X — เพิ่มเมื่อ Y`.

## Check before done
- [ ] An outsider can open it for the first time and understand within 30 seconds.
- [ ] No part, step or layer can be cut with no loss.
- [ ] Every added part has a reason it is needed now, not "just in case".
- [ ] Still complete on correctness, safety and what the user asked for.
- [ ] Duties still clearly separated, not squashed into one place to look short.

## References
- [`references/architecture-and-anti-patterns.md`](references/architecture-and-anti-patterns.md) — open for architecture, specs, plans or designs: architecture do and avoid, extra checks per output type, anti-patterns to reject (future-proofing · layer cake · resume-driven design), wrong and right examples


## reference: architecture-and-anti-patterns.md

# Architecture, specs and anti-patterns · simplify

Open this file for architecture, a spec, a plan or a design that keeps growing parts. It holds the rules not already in `SKILL.md`; each section ends with a line naming the rules `SKILL.md` covers.

## Extra checks before submitting

- **Simplest thing that works:** fewest moving parts, boring proven patterns. Add complexity only when something breaks.
- **Reads in one pass:** no jargon the audience lacks, and the whole thing fits in 2 sentences.
- Any "no" or "not sure" on these or on the `SKILL.md` checklist means: simplify before delivering.

Already in `SKILL.md`: a tired teammate gets it in 6 months (the One rule) · every new component, option or layer has evidence it is needed now (checklist) · nothing can be deleted without losing meaning, deleting beats adding (step 2 and checklist) · an example for every abstract claim (step 3, documents).

## Architecture

Do:
- Monolith first. Split only when a bottleneck is proven.
- A familiar stack and standard patterns: Representational State Transfer (REST), queues, caches.
- 1 source of truth per data type.

Avoid:
- Microservices for small teams · distributed-everything.
- Multi-master databases before you must.
- Event-driven by default. A synchronous call is simpler.

## Documents (BRD · SRS · FSD · ADR)

Business Requirements Document (BRD) · Software Requirements Specification (SRS) · Functional Specification Document (FSD) · Architecture Decision Record (ADR).

Do: sentences of at most 20 words · plain English.

Avoid: marketing-speak ("revolutionary", "best-in-class", "synergy") · walls of text · hedging ("might possibly potentially") · acronym soup.

Already in `SKILL.md`: 1 idea per paragraph · an example for every abstract point · tables for structured data · no undefined jargon (step 3, documents).

## Plans

Do: realistic timelines with buffer · cut scope to fit the time.

Avoid: vague goals ("improve quality") · aspirational dates with no buffer · plans without success metrics.

Already in `SKILL.md`: 3–5 priorities, a named owner per item, measurable success criteria · no 20- or 50-item list with no priority (step 3, plans).

## Designs (user experience (UX) · application programming interface (API))

Do: stay consistent across screens · defaults that work for 80% of users · progressive disclosure (show advanced options only when asked).

Avoid: a novel interaction where a standard one works · a 10-step flow when 3 steps work · required fields with no smart default · hidden features that need a tutorial.

Already in `SKILL.md`: fewest steps to the user's goal · reuse familiar patterns (step 3, designs).

## Anti-patterns to reject

- **Future-proofing:** abstractions for needs that never arrive.
- **"It might scale":** infrastructure for 1M users while you have 1k.
- **Layer cake:** 6 layers where 90% just pass the call through.
- **Resume-driven design:** fancy tech chosen to look sophisticated.
- **Buzzword stacking:** "cloud-native event-driven AI-powered".

## Wrong and right examples

**API description**

Wrong: "This sophisticated, enterprise-grade endpoint leverages state-of-the-art authentication to facilitate the seamless retrieval of user profile data."

Right: "`GET /users/{id}` returns a user profile. Requires a Bearer token. Use `?fields=name,email` to limit the response."

**Sprint goal**

Wrong: "Improve overall product quality and customer satisfaction through various initiatives."

Right: "Reduce login errors by 50% (8% → 4%): fix timeout bug (2d), retry on transient errors (1d), clearer error messages (1d)."

**Architecture for a new feature**

Wrong: "Event-sourced microservice with Command Query Responsibility Segregation (CQRS), Kafka ingestion, Redis cache, and a dedicated auth service."

Right: "Add an endpoint to the existing API. One Postgres table for state. Standard auth middleware. Log to the existing system."

# skill: polished-document-style

Use when a kept document needs headings, tables and theme

# Polished Document Style — headings, tables, callouts, and theme for a kept document

> **Gate before starting (every time):** read the owner's theme → search live references → 3 genuinely different directions → check `no-ai-look` before sending · follow the section "ด่านก่อนลงมือ" of `design-references` (plugin `superuser`) even when a brand exists (the brand controls color and font, the search finds the structure of this piece) · close the work with the line `ด่านก่อนลงมือ:`

> **Boundary:** this skill handles the look; the wording belongs to `human-writing`. Open both for a document people keep to read.

## Use when
- Output is for general readers (managers, executives, clients), needs sign-off, or will be shared widely or converted to PDF/Word · any doc with 3+ sections or 500+ words
- Laying out any document people keep to read (Markdown · Word · PDF), including Thai text in Office files
- Not for: internal notes for the author's own team, scratch notes, code comments · a whole Markdown report that must come out as one .docx → `markdown-report-docx` · a rendered .docx/.pptx/.pdf → `branded-document-design` on top of this skill (this skill governs the markdown source)

## Steps
1. **Find an existing template first.** Check the client's or organization's standard: Word/Google Docs templates the client gave · earlier documents in the project (`docs/`, `ref/`) · format requirements in the TOR or contract. If found, use it (headings, order, field names, running numbers) and say which file it came from. If not, use this skill's structure and say no template was found. Readability applies either way.
2. **Start with the header.** A plain-text H1, then a quote box with version, date, status, author, reviewer, tags, closed with `---` (example in [`references/markdown-patterns.md`](references/markdown-patterns.md)). Formal documents (proposal · formal report · contract · postmortem) open with a cover block: type, version, status, date, author, reviewer, related documents.
   - Status takes only: **Draft** (ร่าง) · **Review** (กำลังรีวิว) · **Approved** (อนุมัติแล้ว) · **Archived** (เก็บถาวร) (`status-report` adds `ยังไม่เริ่ม` for work not begun) · in a Sign-off table the Status column is the signer's: **Approved** · **Review** · **Pending** · **Rejected**.
3. **Headings.** One H1 · H2 numbered (`## 1. Section`) · H3 (`### 1.1 Sub-topic`) · H4 rare. 5+ sections → add a table of contents whose links reach the real headings.
4. **Declare the theme once.** At the end of the header put `<!-- doc-theme: accent=… · ที่มา=… · ยืนยันเมื่อ=YYYY-MM-DD -->`; every tool (`diagram-figures` · `branded-document-design` · `presentation-design`) reads the color from there. To choose a color or put real colors into a figure, .docx, or slides, open [`references/theme-colors.md`](references/theme-colors.md).
5. **Labels are words, never emoji** (emoji in headings and badges signal AI-made, `no-ai-look`):

   | Used for | Words |
   |---|---|
   | Importance | วิกฤต · สูง · กลาง · ต่ำ |
   | Work status | เสร็จ · ทำอยู่ · ติด · รออนุมัติ · ค้างอยู่ |
   | Check result | ผ่าน · ไม่ผ่าน |
   | Text box type | ข้อแนะนำ (Tip) · ข้อควรจำ (Note) · ข้อควรระวัง (Warning) · อันตราย (Critical) · คำถามที่ยังเปิด (Open Question) |

   Yes/no cells may use `✓` `✗` or "ใช่" / "ไม่". Status badge = a bold word (`**Status:** Approved`).
6. **Callouts** are blockquotes with a bold label · 1–3 sentences · one per topic, no stacking · at most 3–5 per page.
7. **Tables** when items have 2+ attributes (bullets whose lines hold several comma-separated values become a table). Left-align text, center checkmarks and numbers, right-align money · `—` for not applicable · short cells (long content goes in paragraphs; cells over 2 sentences become headings) · bold key columns.
   - Compare options or weigh pros and cons → comparison table with a Recommendation column · needs approval → end with a Sign-off table · 5+ abbreviations → glossary. Examples in `references/markdown-patterns.md`.
8. **Figures** in project documents are drawn with `diagram-figures` (house style) and embedded as images; Mermaid (`software-diagrams`) only for quick figures in a README, PR, or code notes. Place the figure after the paragraph that says what question it answers · 1-line caption under it starting **รูปที่ N —** · never repeat a figure; refer to its number.
9. **Lists and code.** Never nest bullets: use sub-headings or a table. Code blocks always name the language; long code gets the file name as a comment on line 1.
10. **Thai in Word · Excel · PDF** (complex-script font · no justify · embed fonts · BOM CSV): open [`references/thai-office.md`](references/thai-office.md) before creating the file.
11. If the skill that writes the document has a template in `assets/`, run `python scripts/check_outline.py <template.md> <document.md>` before sending. It checks headings are complete and in template order, bold fields complete, table headers match, no field unfilled. In a template, end an optional heading or field with `<!-- optional -->`. After editing the checker, run `--self-test` first.

## Check before done
- H1 in plain text · no emoji in any heading, callout, badge, or table
- Header block with version, date, status, authors · TOC if 5+ sections · sections numbered consistently · TOC links work
- Tables where data has 2+ attributes · every flow or relationship has a `diagram-figures` figure, not default Mermaid
- Code blocks have language hints · glossary if 5+ abbreviations · terms used consistently ("user" vs "customer")
- No placeholder text (TBD, TODO, Lorem ipsum); `(รอยืนยัน)` markers listed in the pending-confirmation list are not placeholders, keep them
- Rendered once in the real viewer (Word · PDF · GitHub preview) · item 3 of `no-ai-look` passed

## References
- [`references/markdown-patterns.md`](references/markdown-patterns.md) — open when writing a header, TOC, callout, table, badge, cover block, comparison table, sign-off, or glossary (copy the examples)
- [`references/theme-colors.md`](references/theme-colors.md) — open when choosing the main color or putting colors into a figure, .docx, or slides
- [`references/thai-office.md`](references/thai-office.md) — open when creating Word · Excel · PDF with Thai
- Abbreviation writing → `spell-out-abbreviations`


## reference: markdown-patterns.md

# รูปแบบ markdown พร้อมตัวอย่าง

Markdown code examples for every format that `SKILL.md` refers to, ready to copy and use · the rules on when to use each one live in `SKILL.md`

**สารบัญ:** Document Header · Table of Contents · Callout Boxes · Tables · Figures · Status Badges · Cover Block · Comparison / Decision Tables · Lists · Code Blocks · Approval/Sign-off · Glossary

## Document Header (Always)

Every polished doc MUST start with:

```markdown
# <Document Title>

> **Version:** 1.0 · **Date:** YYYY-MM-DD · **Status:** Draft
> **Authors:** <names> · **Reviewers:** <names>
> **Tags:** `<area>` `<topic>`

---
```

Status values:
- **Draft** — work in progress
- **Review** — under stakeholder review
- **Approved** — signed off
- **Archived** — historical reference

## Table of Contents

**Always add Table of Contents** for docs with 5+ sections:

```markdown
## Table of Contents

1. [Executive Summary](#1-executive-summary)
2. [Scope](#2-scope)
3. [Details](#3-details)
```

## Callout Boxes

Use blockquotes with a bold label — no emoji. 5 ชนิด ชื่อไทยคู่กัน: Tip (ข้อแนะนำ) · Note (ข้อควรจำ) · Warning (ข้อควรระวัง) · Critical (อันตราย) · Open Question (คำถามที่ยังเปิด):

```markdown
> **Tip:** Brief actionable insight.

> **Warning:** Important caveat or limitation.

> **Critical:** Must-read before proceeding.

> **Note:** Additional context or background.

> **Open Question:** Needs decision/clarification.
```

## Tables — When and How

### When to use tables instead of bullets

Use tables when items have **2+ attributes**:

Don't use bullets:
```markdown
- email: string, required, unique
- age: number, optional
- role: enum, required, default "user"
```

Use a table:
```markdown
| Field | Type   | Required | Default | Description       |
|-------|--------|:--------:|:-------:|-------------------|
| email | string | ✓        | —       | Unique login email|
| age   | number | ✗        | —       | Optional          |
| role  | enum   | ✓        | `user`  | Access level      |
```

## Figures (รูปในเอกสาร)

Figures in project documents are drawn with `diagram-figures` (plugin `software-development` · house style) and embedded as image files · use Mermaid only for quick figures in a README · do not use it in documents that are handed on, nor in PRs

```markdown
ลำดับการเรียกเมื่อผู้ใช้กดบันทึกแสดงในรูปที่ 3

![ลำดับการเรียกเมื่อผู้ใช้กดบันทึก](figures/fig-03.png)

**รูปที่ 3 —** ลำดับการเรียกเมื่อผู้ใช้กดบันทึก
```

## Status Badges (Inline)

For key fields in headers/tables:

```markdown
**Status:** Approved
**Priority:** High
**Risk Level:** Medium
**Service Level Agreement (SLA):** < 200ms
```

Multiple badges in a header:

```markdown
> **Approved** · **High Priority** · Owner @alice · Due 2025-03-15
```

## Cover Block Pattern

For formal documents (Business Requirements Document (BRD), Functional Specification Document (FSD), Architecture Decision Record (ADR), postmortem):

```markdown
# <Title>

| | |
|--|--|
| **Document Type** | BRD \| FSD \| ADR \| Postmortem |
| **Version** | 1.2 |
| **Status** | Approved |
| **Date** | 2025-01-15 |
| **Author(s)** | @alice, @bob |
| **Reviewer(s)** | @charlie |
| **Related** | [BRD-001](link), [FSD-005](link) |

---
```

## Comparison / Decision Tables

For trade-off analysis (architect, Project Manager (PM), Search Engine Optimization (SEO) recommendations):

```markdown
| Option | Cost | Effort | Risk | Time-to-Value | Recommendation |
|--------|:----:|:------:|:----:|:-------------:|:--------------:|
| **A**  | ฿80k | Med  | Low  | Fast | **Recommended** |
| B      | ฿40k | Low  | High | Med  | Not recommended |
| C      | ฿150k| High | Low  | Slow | Future consideration |
```

## Lists — When to nest, when to flatten

### Good list
```markdown
- Email is unique across all users
- Passwords must be 8+ characters with mixed case
- Sessions expire after 30 days of inactivity
```

### Bad list (over-nested)
```markdown
- Users
  - Email
    - Must be unique
    - Required
  - Password
    - 8+ chars
    - Mixed case
```

→ Should be a table instead.

## Code Blocks

Always specify language:

````markdown
```typescript
const user: User = { id: 1, email: 'a@b.com' };
```

```bash
npm install
```

```sql
SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = $1;
```
````

For long blocks, put the file name in a comment on the first line:

```typescript
// src/services/auth.ts
export async function login(email: string, password: string) {
  // ...
}
```

## Approval/Sign-off Section (End of Doc)

For documents needing formal approval:

```markdown
## Sign-off

| Role | Name | Status | Date |
|------|------|:------:|------|
| Product Owner | @alice | Approved | 2025-01-15 |
| Tech Lead | @bob | Review | — |
| QA Lead | @charlie | Pending | — |
| Security | @dave | Rejected | 2025-01-14 |
```

## Glossary Section

For docs with 5+ technical terms:

```markdown
## Glossary

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| **API** | Application Programming Interface |
| **JWT** | JSON Web Token, used for stateless auth |
| **SLA** | Service Level Agreement |
```

Define acronyms on first use, then add to glossary.


## reference: thai-office.md

# Thai Office documents

Applies to every Word · Excel · PDF file that contains Thai, whether a script builds it or a person makes it by hand. Details and helpers are in `branded-document-design`.

- Word treats Thai as a complex script, so it has separate font, size and bold fields from Latin. If you set only the Latin field, the Thai text does not change. Set both.
- Do not justify Thai paragraphs. Thai has no spaces between words, so Word stretches the letter spacing and leaves gaps. The exception is a thesis guide that requires Thai Distributed.
- Never use a mono font for Thai text, because Consolas and Cascadia have no Thai letters. Use mono only for codes, keys and numbers.
- Always embed fonts when exporting PDF. Otherwise a machine without the font substitutes another one and the tone marks float.
- Save a CSV that Thai users will open in Excel as UTF-8 with BOM (byte order mark). Otherwise the Thai text turns to garbage.
- Before you say it is done, render every page to an image and look at it. Overflowing tables, headings stranded at the bottom of a page and floating tone marks do not show up in the code.


## reference: theme-colors.md

# Document theme color table

This file says who controls the color of each part of a document, and what the house default colors are. Use it when you must put real colors into a figure, a .docx file or slides.

## Declare the theme — decide once, use everywhere in that document

One document passes through several skills: markdown (`polished-document-style`) · figures from `diagram-figures` ·
.docx files from `branded-document-design` · slides from `presentation-design` (all three are in plugin `software-development`).
If each one picks its own color, the reader gets a document with figures in one color, headings in another, and slides in a third.

**Markdown is the main source (source of truth), so the theme is declared here** — put it at the end of the document header or in a file beside it:

```markdown
<!-- doc-theme: accent=<สีหลัก> · ที่มา=<แบรนด์ลูกค้า / เสนอจากเนื้องาน> · ยืนยันเมื่อ=YYYY-MM-DD -->
```

(Keys: `accent` = main color · `ที่มา` = source (client brand / proposed from the work's content) · `ยืนยันเมื่อ` = confirmed on.)

**The main color comes from the work's content, not from a tool's default.**
If a brand color already exists, use it. If not, search for references per `design-references` (plugin `superuser`) of type `document` and extract the color from the chosen work · if live search is not possible, use the house default, write `(รอยืนยัน)` (awaiting confirmation), carry on without stopping to ask, and propose a tone that fits the work's content in the report.
(Backup: the table matching work content to color tones is in `colour-by-domain` of skill `diagram-figures` (plugin `software-development`).)

Markdown itself has no color, so use labels and font weight instead. Diagrams, figures, .docx files and slides read the value from `doc-theme`. If `doc-theme` has not declared a work-specific accent, use the house default. Both tables are below.

**Status words do not depend on the theme** — วิกฤต (critical) · ผ่าน (pass) use the same words in every document. Status colors in .docx files and slides are below.

## Who controls the color of which part

| Part of the document | Who controls the color | Read the value from |
|---|---|---|
| Headings, tables, text boxes in markdown | Markdown has no color; use bold labels and font weight instead | — |
| Mermaid diagrams | `diagram-figures` → `references/engine-mermaid.md` (README · PR: `software-diagrams` item 2 in plugin `software-development`) | `doc-theme` |
| Figures that are image files | `diagram-figures` (plugin `software-development`) | `doc-theme` |
| Exported .docx / .pdf files | `branded-document-design` (plugin `software-development`) items 0–1 | `doc-theme` |
| Slides | `presentation-design` (plugin `software-development`) | `doc-theme` |

## House default

If `doc-theme` has not declared a work-specific accent, every skill uses this set as the default, so figures, documents and slides share one palette from the start. This is the same set as `presentation-design` and `branded-document-design`:

| token | Value | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| brand | `#2A78D6` | Main color · headings · accent lines |
| brand-deep | `#2A4C86` | Table headers · H2 · system names |
| brand-2 | `#6A5CD6` | Secondary accent (purple) |
| tint | `#EDF1FB` | Table header background · highlight box background |
| ink / body | `#333B4A` / `#414957` | Headings / body text |
| muted / faint | `#7D8492` / `#A9AEB9` | Captions / notes |
| line | `#E4E7EE` | Borders · connector lines |
| exception | `#C77A11` | A path/zone that is not the main route (always different from brand) |
| Font | Tahoma (documents/slides) · Noto Sans Thai → Tahoma (images) | Both Thai and English |

Once a work-specific accent is declared, use it in place of brand, and compute the other colors from that accent.

# skill: branded-document-design

Use when a Word, PowerPoint or PDF or its cover must look designed

# Branded Document Design — .docx / .pptx / .pdf that looks intentionally designed

> **Pre-work gate (`ด่านก่อนลงมือ`, every time):** read the owner's theme → search live for reference designs → 3 genuinely different directions → check `no-ai-look` before sending · follow the section "ด่านก่อนลงมือ" of `design-references` (plugin `superuser`) even when a brand exists (the brand controls color and fonts; the search is for this piece's structure) · close the job with the line `ด่านก่อนลงมือ:`

> **One rule:** an exported document has one color set, and one set of type sizes and spacing that is the same on every page. It must not look like someone opened Word and just typed.

## Use when
- The output is a .docx / .pptx / .pdf (quotation · business plan · report · contract · SRS) that a customer, executive, or another team will open, or that must be signed off or attached to a contract
- A document set needs its own cover from the logo shape or a real mockup, or covers look alike across projects → step 3 and `references/cover-design.md`
- Mixed Thai–English documents (they break easily if fonts are not fully set)
- The same kind of document is issued repeatedly and every copy should look the same
- Not for: markdown output → `polished-document-style` · reading or extracting a received Office file → `anthropic-skills:docx` · `xlsx` · `pptx` · `pdf` · diagrams in markdown → `markdown-visuals` · a whole-book report from one Markdown file → `markdown-report-docx`

Order: write the content as markdown first (`polished-document-style`), then render it with this skill. Always fix content in the markdown (the source).

Install before use: `pip install python-docx python-pptx` · LibreOffice (`soffice`) to convert to PDF · `pdftoppm` (poppler) to convert to images.

## Steps
1. **Colors.** If the source markdown has a `doc-theme`, use it: do not ask, do not set a new one (`polished-document-style`, "ธีมของเอกสาร"). Otherwise look in the order in `diagram-figures` item 5 (`doc-theme` → brand colors in code, logo, brand kit → nothing). If there is nothing, search live for reference designs per `design-references` (plugin `superuser`), type `document`, then extract colors from the chosen work (stored palette library when live search is impossible). If live search is impossible, use the house color `#2A78D6`, write `(รอยืนยัน)` in the report, and carry on without asking; put a tone suggested by the content in the report for the user to choose later ([`references/palette-examples.md`](references/palette-examples.md)). A customer's brand colors always win. Write the colors back into `doc-theme` in the markdown so document, figures, and slides match.
   - **One main color.** All light and dark shades are computed from it. Only the status colors (success · warning · error) are independent and keep their meaning.
2. **Continue the look of the brand or app, before the first render.** The skill's defaults (Tahoma · solid color band cover · lines in every table cell) are the floor, not the deliverable look.
   - Is there an identity already? Check the brand kit (`graphic-design:brand-kit`), `assets/logo/`, `docs/design/`, a mockup that passed the beauty gate (score in `docs/BUILD-PLAN.md`), field `doc-theme` in `docs/README.md`. If yes, use the same logo (cover + page header), colors, and patterns as the app. If no, follow step 1.
   - Do 1 direction first. Only if the user is not wowed or asks for several, do 3 directions, have 2 outside reviewers score them, and run the document beauty gate (`ด่านสวย`, ceiling 3 rounds, record every score in `docs/BUILD-PLAN.md`): [`references/identity-and-gate.md`](references/identity-and-gate.md).
   - Work on the render script, not on .docx files one by one; render every copy.
   - **Fonts:** the brand's Thai font installed and embedded (`embed_fonts`) · Tahoma when embedding is impossible · never set Thai text in a mono font (no Thai letters in Cascadia/Consolas); mono is for code, keys, and numbers.
   - Figures in documents, beauty-gate rules, cover: [`references/word-layout.md`](references/word-layout.md), section at the end.
3. **Cover for this document set.** For a software document set (BRD · SRS · FSD · ARCH) whose cover must come from the logo shape or a real mockup, follow [`references/cover-design.md`](references/cover-design.md) (page system · registry · checks · cover engine `scripts/cover-engine/`). If the default cover looks like another job's, do 1 direction first; only if the user is not wowed or asks for several, run the 3-direction, 2-of-3 vote in [`references/cover-vote.md`](references/cover-vote.md).
4. **Tokens, never hardcode colors outside them.** `brand` · `brand_2` · `brand_deep` · `brand_tint` · `brand_tint_2` · `text` · `text_body` · `text_muted` · `line` + 6 status colors (success · info · warning · error · accent · neutral) that do not change with the brand. Set the values once with `use_brand(...)`.
   - Choose colors by meaning (red = danger/real error only); same meaning set as diagrams.
   - Contrast: body text and `text_muted` on the background ≥ 4.5:1 · H2 and table headers (`brand_deep`) ≥ 7:1 · H1 and KPI numbers (`brand`, large) ≥ 3:1 · `use_brand()` stops if it fails · in black and white the hierarchy must still read · if it fails, adjust darkness, not the color.
   - Text is never pure black (use `text_body`) · no type size outside the scale (Word body 11pt · slides 17pt).
   - Full token table, color meanings, type scale, elements: [`references/tokens-and-type.md`](references/tokens-and-type.md).
5. **Fonts and Thai.** Word treats Thai as a complex script: never set font/size/bold by hand; use `style_run()` in `brandkit.py` (sets `w:szCs` `w:bCs` `w:iCs` and all 4 slots of `w:rFonts`). If Latin and Thai fonts differ, set `bk.FONT` and `bk.LATIN_FONT`, then call `bk.thai_runs(doc.element.body)` and on every header/footer before `save()`. Line spacing 1.3–1.35 (Tahoma) · never justify Thai paragraphs · to send a PDF, export from real Word or check by eye (LibreOffice breaks Thai differently) · Linux has no Tahoma, use Loma/Sarabun · ReportLab places tone marks wrongly. Traps and embedding: [`references/thai-fonts.md`](references/thai-fonts.md).
6. **Word page structure.** Cover (project logo and mockup exist → project-specific cover per step 3; else the default) → table of contents → body (H1 numbered, keep-with-next on headings) → sign-off table · footer "หน้า N" centered, gray 9pt · A4, content width 17 cm = 9638 twips (`BODY_TWIPS`) so column widths add up. Full structure and dark cover (`doc.cover(..., style="night")`): [`references/word-layout.md`](references/word-layout.md).
   - Cover background image and logo never go in the first-page header (Word shows them faded); anchor them to the cover's first paragraph. Inner-page table headers never use a full-width solid dark fill.
7. **Use the elements** `cover()` · `table()` · `pill_table()` · `kpi_row()` · `callout()` · `figure()` · `code()` · `signoff()` (methods in `references/tokens-and-type.md`). At most 3–5 callouts per 10 pages · KPI strip of 3–5 cells · a table over 6 columns goes on a landscape page (`landscape_section()`).
8. **Use brandkit.** `from brandkit import BrandDoc, use_brand, to_pdf` (put `scripts/` on the path) · slides → `brandkit_pptx.BrandDeck` · speaking deck → `brandkit_stage.StageDeck` (default: `accent`/`bg` from the source work per `presentation-design` `references/deck-theme.md`, `source_palette.py` prints the `StageDeck(...)` line; light `FFFFFF` with `block=True`, dark only if the source is dark; no color at all → `#2A78D6` on `FFFFFF` + `(รอยืนยัน)`). Sample code and methods: [`references/brandkit-usage.md`](references/brandkit-usage.md), `references/api.md`.
9. **Look at every page before delivery.** Render to PDF, convert to images, open each page (Read tool): the code cannot show tables overflowing the margin, stranded headings, floating tone marks. Commands and the 7-point checklist: [`references/visual-check.md`](references/visual-check.md).
10. Before sending, go through item 3 of `no-ai-look` (HTML work: run its script; the eye gate 3.2 must also pass, web pages answer items 10–14).

**Hard rules (covers):**
- A project cover shows its project by logo shape or a real screen at a glance, not by colour alone.
- Never draw a fake UI on a cover. Use a real mockup screenshot. No logo or mockup yet: stop and make the logo first.
- Ask before creating or editing files outside the project (e.g. `cover-registry.md`).
- Install fonts only after asking, and only with `COVER_INSTALL_FONTS=1`.

## Check before done
- Avoid: Word's built-in Heading styles (use `h1()/h2()/h3()`) · thick black default table lines (use 0.5pt `line`) · pure black text · bold table headers with no fill · letting Word choose column widths (`fixed_widths()`) · too many emoji · a file never rendered for a look · the skill's default look when the app already has an identity · a 2000px-wide figure on a 17 cm page (text ends near 5pt) · a decorative cover image nobody said wows · a .docx without the source markdown. Reasons: [`references/anti-patterns.md`](references/anti-patterns.md)
- Every page was opened and looked at · colors written back to `doc-theme` · the line `ด่านก่อนลงมือ:` closes the job

## reference: anti-patterns.md

# Anti-patterns — reasons and what to use instead

The short headings are in `SKILL.md`.

- **Using Word's built-in Heading styles** — they override the colors you set. Use `h1()/h2()/h3()`,
  which set `outlineLvl` themselves, so the table of contents (TOC) still shows the headings.
- **Thick black default table borders** — the document looks dated at once. Use lines in the `line` color at 0.5pt between rows (under the header row is the 1.5pt brand line).
- **Pure black text** — use `text_body`, a dark gray. The body text becomes much softer.
- **Bold table headers with no fill color** — when a table spans pages, readers cannot tell where it starts.
- **Letting Word work out column widths** — always call `fixed_widths()`.
  Otherwise the code column ends up as wide as the detail column.
- **Too many emoji** — 1 per callout is enough. Do not put one in every heading.
- **Sending the file without ever rendering it** — see item 6.
- **Creating the .docx without keeping the source markdown** — you cannot edit it next time.


## reference: api.md

# brandkit API — method reference

Every method returns the object it created (paragraph / table / slide), so you can customize it further.

## Contents

1. [brandkit.py — Word (.docx)](#brandkitpy--word-docx)
2. [brandkit_pptx.py — slides (.pptx)](#brandkit_pptxpy--slides-pptx)
3. [brandkit_stage.py — Stage deck (.pptx)](#brandkit_stagepy--stage-deck-pptx)
4. [Column width formulas (Word)](#column-width-formulas-word)

## brandkit.py — Word (.docx)

### Create a document

```python
BrandDoc(path_template=None, page="A4", margins_cm=(2.2, 2.0, 2.2, 2.0),
         footer_text="หน้า")
```

| Parameter | Meaning |
|-------------|----------|
| `path_template` | A .docx/.dotx file used as the template (already holds the organization's header/logo) |
| `page` | `"A4"` or `"Letter"` |
| `margins_cm` | (top, right, bottom, left) |
| `footer_text` | Prefix before the page number · `""` = bare number |

### Page-level blocks

| Method | Note |
|-------|----------|
| `cover(title, subtitle, meta, note, logo, logo_width_cm=None, eyebrow=None, meta_rows=None, top_space_pt=24, page_break=True, style="light", art_colors=None)` | The logo accepts .png and .emf, but **.svg does not work in python-docx**; convert to PNG first (`rsvg-convert -w 600` or `cairosvg`) |
| `cover(..., style="night")` | **Full-page dark cover** (see the example `examples/example_srs-preview.png`): dark gray background `#1C1C22` + a faint brand-colored glow · `logo` (omitted = no logo) small at top left, 4.6 cm wide · `eyebrow` → document title (32pt · if longer than 2 lines, reduce to 26pt) → `subtitle` → a glow line the full width of the text · `meta_rows` short values (≤18 characters, at most 4 values) go in a 4-cell table, the rest as label/value rows · `note` last · the cover has no footer · `art_colors=(color1, color2, color3)` colors of the glow line from left to right and of the background glow (default `brand_2` → `brand` → light `brand`) · the background image/logo/line are anchored to a paragraph in the body, not the header · needs numpy + pillow (`cover_art.py`) · `logo_width_cm` default 2.6 (light) / 4.6 (night) |
| `toc(heading="สารบัญ", levels="1-3")` | Inserts a TOC field; then in Word press **Ctrl+A then F9** so the entries appear (it is empty when created) |
| `page_break()` | |
| `landscape_section()` | Opens a landscape section for wide tables |

### Headings and text

| Method | Result |
|-------|---------|
| `h1(text)` `h2(text)` `h3(text)` | 16 / 12.5 / 11.5 pt · bold · brand / brand_deep / text · sets `outlineLvl` so the TOC sees them |
| `para(text, size, color, bold, italic, align, space_after)` | `align` = `"center"｜"right"｜"justify"` (do not justify Thai) |
| `rich([(text, opts), ...])` | Several formats in one paragraph, e.g. `[("สถานะ: ", {"bold": True}), ("อนุมัติ", {"color": "green"})]` |
| `bullets([...], style="List Bullet")` | `style="List Number"` for numbered lists |
| `code(text)` | Gray-background code block |

### Tables and data

| Method | Note |
|-------|----------|
| `table(headers, rows, widths=None, zebra=False, align=None, first_col_bold=False, size=None, header_style="tint")` | `widths` in twips totaling **9638** (`BODY_TWIPS`) for A4 with 2 cm margins · `align` = a list per column · `header_style="tint"` (default) header filled with `brand` mixed 80% with white, bold `brand_deep` text, no top line, a single 1.5pt `brand` line under the header, thin row lines, no vertical lines · `"classic"` = the old style (`brand_tint` header, thin gray grid) |
| `pill_table(headers, rows, status_col, palette, widths)` | `palette = {"เสร็จ": "green", "ค้าง": "red"}` · available tones: green blue amber red violet grey |
| `kpi_row([(value, label), ...])` | Exactly 3–5 cells |
| `signoff([(role, name), ...])` | Sign-off table |

### Other

| Method | Note |
|-------|----------|
| `callout(kind, title, body)` | kind = `tip｜note｜warning｜critical｜success｜question` |
| `figure(image_path, caption, width_cm=15.5, number=None)` | `number=1` prefixes the caption with "รูปที่ 1 — " (Figure 1) |
| `save(path)` | |

### Module-level functions

| Function | Use when |
|----------|---------|
| `use_brand(**tokens)` | Change the whole color set; must be called **before** creating `BrandDoc` |
| `style_run(run, size, color, bold, italic, mono)` | Set the font yourself (complex-script is already covered) |
| `shade(cell, token)` · `left_accent(cell, token, size)` | Fill a cell / add a colored bar on its left |
| `fixed_widths(table, widths)` | Force column widths |
| `set_borders(table)` · `row_borders(table)` · `no_borders(table)` · `cell_border(cell, edge, color, size)` | `row_borders` = horizontal lines only · `cell_border(..., color=None)` = no line on that side |
| `mix(color, other="FFFFFF", amount=0.5)` | Mix colors to make lighter/darker shades from the palette |
| `repeat_header(row)` · `keep_with_next(paragraph)` | |
| `add_field(paragraph, "PAGE")` | Insert a Word field |
| `to_pdf(docx_path, outdir)` | Calls LibreOffice to convert to PDF |

## brandkit_pptx.py — slides (.pptx)

```python
BrandDeck(template=None)      # 16:9 (13.333 × 7.5 inches)
```

| Method | Resulting slide |
|-------|-------------|
| `title_slide(title, subtitle, meta)` | Light blue background + a brand divider line |
| `section(title, kicker=None)` | Vertical brand bar on the left + section name |
| `bullets_slide(title, items, subtitle=None)` | Title + purple dash under the title + 17pt bullets |
| `kpi_slide(title, items, subtitle=None)` | Number cards |
| `table_slide(title, headers, rows, col_widths, subtitle, status_col, palette)` | `col_widths` are proportions, e.g. `[1, 4, 2, 2]` |
| `image_slide(title, image_path, caption, subtitle)` | Image centered on the slide, fitted to the frame automatically |
| `quote_slide(text, source)` | Quote/conclusion slide |
| `save(path)` | |

**Limits to know**

- Every slide is built from the blank layout (`slide_layouts[6]`), so there are no placeholders to edit in PowerPoint
  as in a normal template. If the customer will edit a lot themselves, pass `template=` as the organization's .pptx file instead.
- Tables in python-pptx have no API to turn off borders directly. If you want a table without lines, arrange text boxes instead.
- Table row height is a minimum. Long text pushes the row taller by itself, so leave room.

---

## brandkit_stage.py — Stage deck (.pptx)

```python
StageDeck(accent="2A78D6", bg="09090A", project="", template=None,
          head_font="Chakra Petch", body_font="IBM Plex Sans Thai", block=False, **colors)
# accent / bg = main color and background color from the project's design · colors = colors the project already fixed, e.g. text="1B2430"
# block=True = cover() and section() are a solid main-color full sheet, text on it gets ≥ 4.5:1 (white, near black or black)
```

Every sheet except the cover and chapter divider has: a main-color square + category name (`kicker`) · 28 pt slide title · a line at the foot of the page · `PROJECT · category` · 2-digit page number

| Method | Resulting slide |
|-------|-------------|
| `cover(title, lines, meta, logo=None, mark=None)` | 60 pt title + a main-color dash · `lines[1]` is in the main color · `mark` = a large faint symbol on the right (omitted = a faint ring) |
| `section(number, title, note)` | Chapter divider: a large number in the main color |
| `figure(kicker, title, image, caption, subtitle)` | Full-sheet diagram image (rendered with the same `#bg=` as the deck) |
| `compare(kicker, title, headers, rows, widths=(1, 1.85, 1.95))` | Table with row separator lines · column 1 gray, 2 bold white, 3 body text · at most 5 rows |
| `stats(kicker, title, items, subtitle)` | 2–4 big numbers + a sample question/answer under each number |
| `steps(kicker, title, rows, example_head, note)` | Numbered steps · `rows = [(name, what it does, example)]` at most 6 steps |
| `points(kicker, title, points, image, caption, side, side_caption)` | Image on the left + gist with a main-color dash · `side` = a small image on the right, e.g. a QR code |
| `statement(kicker, text, sub)` | A single statement centered on the sheet |
| `save(path)` | |

Color helpers: `make_theme(accent, bg)` returns the whole color set · `fit(color, bg)` adjusts lightness while keeping vividness until readable on that background · `is_dark(bg)` · `contrast(a, b)`
